identify.client: Pennywhistle Software Ltd, a fictional company of fourteen people that sells an email-campaign product to small retailers, about 900 paying customers, a third of them in the European Union; invented by the practice for testing
identify.acting: the company's head of engineering, for Pennywhistle Software Ltd
identify.counterparty: the maintainer of Chhoto URL, as seller
identify.confidentiality: the code is public; the fact of the negotiation and the price are confidential until closing

situation.subject: the Chhoto URL link shortener: the copyright in the source code, the project name and the project's domain, with the maintainer contracted for 40 hours of handover over three months. The buyer will run one instance per customer as a branded short-link add-on to its email product
situation.price: $60,000, of which $15,000 is held back for six months against the documentation proving accurate; the price was set from the README and the documentation pages alone, on the assumption that they are accurate
situation.structure: asset purchase with a six-month holdback; the seller warrants ownership of the code and the accuracy of the published documentation
situation.timetable: 30 days to closing; the buyer wants the add-on on sale in the following quarter

background.target: the public Chhoto URL repository at the commit the seller named, with its documentation pages and the project website
background.claim_sources: the README, the command-line, security and tools documentation pages, and the project website's home page
background.known: one of the buyer's engineers has run the container on a laptop and it worked; nobody at the buyer reads Rust well. The buyer's two operations engineers will deploy and configure every instance from the documentation, not from the code

assessment.paying_for: a link shortener that (1) records nothing about the people who click a link beyond a count of hits, so the buyer can offer it to European customers without a new data-processing assessment; (2) is small enough to run one instance per customer on the buyer's cheapest virtual machines, 256 MB of memory each, which is what makes the add-on profitable at $4 a month; (3) can be deployed and configured by two operations engineers working from the documentation alone; and (4) the buyer will own outright
assessment.price_movers: any logging or tracking of visitors beyond the hit count; memory, image-size or resource figures materially worse than stated, because at 900 instances the hosting cost is the margin; a security or hardening measure the documentation describes as present or on by default that is absent or off; environment variables, defaults, command-line options or API routes that do not behave as documented, because the holdback is against exactly that; a documented feature (custom slugs, expiry, the command-line client, the API) that is missing or partial
assessment.walk_away: the seller not owning the code, or a licence on the code or a dependency that stops the buyer selling a hosted service built on it; personal data of visitors stored or sent anywhere; a dependency on a database or outside service the buyer cannot run on its own machines

recommendation.scope: all five claim sources; the buyer asked that claims about the project's community (stars, contributors, translations, who else uses it) not be tested, because nothing the buyer pays for rests on them

notes: INVENTED BY THE PRACTICE 2026-09-18 as test data for the tier stage. No such buyer, deal or conversation exists.
the buyer said it has no interest in the project's popularity, its history, or how it compares with other shorteners
the buyer said the web interface's appearance does not matter; its customers will never see it, only the buyer's operations engineers will
the buyer said it will not use the Helm chart or any Kubernetes material; it deploys with Docker Compose only
